title: ESP32 deep sleep and timer wake-up

spans.text: Deep sleep reduces power use in battery-powered ESP32 devices that wait for long periods. Most CPU and RAM state is lost; selected RTC memory and wake sources can remain available. A timer, supported GPIO, or sensors on some chips can wake the device. Wake-up restarts the program at

; ordinary RAM variables do not retain their values.

A typical cycle is: read a sensor, save or send the result, stop radio activity, configure a wake source, then sleep. This example wakes by timer after 10 seconds.
retains the counter in RTC memory on supported chips. The timer API uses microseconds; check its return status.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: Wake pins, retained RTC memory, current draw, and Arduino APIs vary by chip, board, and core version. Since wake-up restarts the program, the same code may immediately enter sleep again. Measure actual board power and check its pinout before relying on a wake source.
